title: Nuevo Laredo Reports No Emergencies After Weekend Rains Bring About 67 mm
excerpt: About 67 millimeters of rain fell in Nuevo Laredo over the weekend, but Civil Protection reported no stranded vehicles and no rain-related emergency calls, with main avenues and bridges staying open.
content:
Weekend rain in Nuevo Laredo brought about 67 millimeters of precipitation, but the city came through it without a single stranded vehicle or rain-related emergency call, according to the city's Civil Protection and Fire Department.

The department said it monitored weather conditions and key points around the city through the weekend, according to IPC Noticias. Some underpasses had standing water, but the main avenues and bridges stayed open and no flooding was reported that threatened traffic.

Storm drains, cattle guards and natural and built drainage channels kept working at full capacity to move the water out, according to the department. Among the channels in that system are Canal Concordia, Canal Voluntad 4, Lomas del Río, Pancho Villa and Cavazos Lerma, along with Arroyo El Coyote and others.

With cool conditions continuing and more rain possible, Civil Protection is asking residents to keep drains, rooftops and patios clear of debris to prevent water from pooling, to drive carefully and slow down on wet pavement, and to avoid crossing streets, streams or underpasses with heavy water flow.

Residents who need help from Civil Protection and Fire can call 867 712 8911, 867 712 2124 or 867 712 3030, or reach the city's CIGA service center at 072. In an emergency, the number is 911.

Source: IPC Noticias, November 16, 2026.
